findings.title: Worker stdout EOF enters a wait that cannot observe the stop flag
findings.evidence: The fake worker remains alive and its output immediately returns EOF. run exits the queue loop and calls child.wait() without a timeout. The probe intercepts that call instead of starting a process. SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers only set stopping, so this wait has no route to stop_worker until the worker exits or wait raises.
findings.trigger: A worker closes stdout/stderr while remaining alive. Whether the externally prepared PC worker can do this is not established.
findings.impact: Unattended cancellation and cleanup can stall indefinitely after EOF. No claim that this happened on the PC.
findings.smallestSafeFix: After EOF, keep polling/waiting with a timeout and honor stopping before the final reap. Add an EOF-while-alive fixture to the existing supervisor suite.
existingChecks: tests/windows/unattended_build_test.py:189-234 tests stop/driver cleanup; 269-283 tests stop and competing lock, but stdout stays open.

findings.title: An interrupted source download becomes a reusable pristine cache entry
findings.evidence: fetch writes curl output directly to CACHE/path. The fake curl writes partial bytes and raises. A second fetch sees is_file and returns those bytes without a new download or validation. Offline prepare also only checks file existence.
findings.impact: An interrupted fetch can poison subsequent source fixtures. Patch anchor checks may reject many such files, but cache existence is not proof of pinned source. check_resources also executes cached generate_grd.py.
findings.smallestSafeFix: Use a unique temporary download, validate success before atomic rename, and bind pristine cache entries to reviewed version/content hashes. Reuse the staging pattern already present in check_breezer_omnibox.py:46-60 and package_breezer_ai.py:32-48; add an interrupted-fetch fake test.
existingChecks: check_ai_overlay.py:128-162 checks overlay idempotence, identity and anchor drift; it does not test download interruption.
check_breezer_omnibox.py already uses a temporary file and rename.
findings.reproduction: build-tools-audit-probe.py: cacheRetry. No curl or network was invoked.

findings.title: Transport summary accepts an invalid footprint sample as a measurement
findings.evidence: A fabricated passed report with the expected pair counts but usage schema 999, PID 999 instead of trial PID 123, status error and negative physicalFootprintBytes yields a median of -1 MiB. The summarizer takes usage.processes[0] without checking identity, status or numeric bounds.
findings.impact: Malformed or misattributed footprint samples can enter published-looking summaries. This does not invalidate any existing raw report without checking that report.
findings.smallestSafeFix: Before summarizing require schema 1, exactly one successful process matching after.pid, a finite nonnegative safe integer footprint, consistent before/after identity and valid metrics. Require producer-side probe validation too. Reuse the identity validation approach in benchmark_browsers.mjs:124-165 rather than creating another measurement harness.
existingChecks: summarize_native_transport.py already rejects mixed runtime/source hashes and missing/repeated pairs.
benchmark_browsers.mjs has stricter footprint identity/status validation. No transport-summary test was found among inspected assigned scripts or relevant test filenames.
findings.reproduction: build-tools-audit-probe.py: invalidTransport; raw input is build-tools-audit-invalid-transport.json.

findings.title: Browser diagnostic logs grow without a byte limit
findings.evidence: Both helpers append every stderr/stdout chunk to arrays until cleanup. Buffer.concat duplicates retained data when producing a log. Slicing the concatenated string in the blocker helper only bounds the displayed tail, not retained buffers or concatenation.
findings.impact: Long or noisy diagnostic runs can consume increasing harness memory. These arrays belong to the Node harness, so bounding them does not reduce sustained browser RAM.
findings.smallestSafeFix: Stream full logs to an owned artifact with backpressure and retain only a capped byte tail for errors. Test a fake noisy stream and exact cap without timing measurements.
existingChecks: benchmark_native_transport.mjs:45-47 already keeps a bounded stderr tail.
The supervisor uses queue.Queue(maxsize=128), 65536-character reads and a 30-entry error deque.
findings.reproduction: Static complete-file read. No browser or allocation stress test run.

findings.title: Checkpointing rehashes both complete Ninja journals on every interval
findings.evidence: Two fake checkpoint calls invoke digest four times, once per whole .ninja_log and .ninja_deps per checkpoint. Hashing is streamed, so it does not retain the whole files. os.sync also runs on every checkpoint. The supervisor does not use these journal hashes to restore or authorize resume.
findings.impact: Potential repeated I/O during large builds, especially large .ninja_deps. No CPU/time/RSS saving measured. This is build-only work.
findings.smallestSafeFix: Keep action checkpoints and durable state, but consider recording journal size/mtime during intermediate checkpoints and reserve whole-file hashes for stopped/final receipts. Do not replace integrity checks without deciding which receipt requires them.
existingChecks: tests/windows/unattended_build_test.py:70-125 verifies real Ninja checkpoint, interruption and preserved output mtimes. It asserts .ninja_log metadata presence, not a dependency on journal hashes for resume.
BuildProgress.psm1:94-107 already avoids repeated full-log reads.
findings.reproduction: build-tools-audit-probe.py: checkpointJournalReads. No real journal, os.sync or benchmark ran.

findings.title: Diagnostic timeout can clear the only SIGKILL watchdog before the child has exited
findings.evidence: The 15-second bounded promise can reject before the 20-second watchdog. finally clears that watchdog, disconnects IPC, then sends SIGTERM without awaiting close or escalating. A child ignoring SIGTERM can remain alive, retaining pipes and the diagnostic process.
findings.impact: Failure-path helper leakage or hung offline diagnostics. Existing success-path close assertions do not cover an unresponsive child.
findings.smallestSafeFix: Centralize cleanup: send SIGTERM, await close under a deadline, then SIGKILL and reap. Keep the kill watchdog armed until close is observed. Add a fake-child lifecycle check or bounded disposable-child regression when operational tests are permitted.
existingChecks: benchmark_native_transport.mjs:69-72 checks code zero and decoder.finish on the success path.
findings.reproduction: Static complete-file read only; no host process was started.

findings.title: Authored-source inventory omits the native C measurement probe
findings.evidence: The CODE suffix set lacks .c. script/macos_process_usage.c exists and benchmark_browsers.mjs reads and compiles it as its physical-footprint probe. It is absent from the assigned 62-file inventory.
findings.impact: A complete claim over this inventory is narrower than a complete authored-code audit, especially for measurement validity.
findings.smallestSafeFix: Include .c in the inventory suffix set, regenerate through the coordinator, and assign a complete review of the added probe. Review other authored-language suffixes against the actual checkout before claiming whole-repository coverage.
existingChecks: check_efficiency_coverage.py validates only inventory entries and reviewer claims, so it cannot detect an omitted source path.
findings.reproduction: Offline existence and inventory suffix comparison. The C file contents were not read in this assigned audit.

findings.title: Migration hashes packet bytes then rereads them for source replacement
findings.evidence: The validation loop hashes replacement files but stores Path objects. The mutation loop rereads replacement bytes. A packet edit between those operations could write unvalidated data and update the plan before the final mismatch check.
findings.trigger: A concurrent writer changes a staged packet during migration. PC stopped-worker enforcement does not by itself make packet files immutable. No such writer or incident was observed.
findings.impact: Final validation detects mismatch but only after source/plan mutation. Ordinary interruption between known before/after values remains recoverable as tested.
findings.smallestSafeFix: Capture replacement bytes once during preflight, validate their hash, and write that captured data. Preserve before/after pin guards and backups. Add a mutation-between-validation-and-write case to existing migration tests.
existingChecks: tests/windows/memory_update_test.py:95-99,131-142 covers interrupted known-version writes; 124-129,144-168 covers corruption present before preflight. It does not change the packet during preflight.
findings.reproduction: Not executed: migration/deployment scripts were not run, including against fixture source. This is a source-based race hypothesis.
